title: Hosted-to-Dedicated Transition Playbook: customer migration and runbook
author: Maya Chen
summary: A practical, step-by-step playbook to migrate customers from Redwood hosted inference to Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity with minimal disruption and predictable economics.
audience: Solutions engineers, customer success, platform engineers, account executives
objectives: 1) Provide a deterministic migration path from Hosted to Dedicated. 2) Align teams on testing, billing implications, and rollback triggers. 3) Document operational runbook and observability checks for day-1 post-migration.
prerequisites:
- Customer has signed a Dedicated contract and capacity commitment.
- Customer environment inventory (models, endpoints, traffic patterns) exported.
- Access to customer account, billing contacts, and networking details (VPC peering/subnets where applicable).
rollout_phases:
1. Planning and sizing
   - Collect per-route QPS, 95/99 latency, average sequence length.
   - Run cost simulator (redwood-optimize) with customer's historical trace.
2. Staging and compatibility test
   - Provision a Dedicated staging pool.
   - Smoke-test model variants, quantization profiles, and function/tool-calling paths.
3. Pilot customer traffic
   - Route 5-10% traffic with weighted routing and monitoring.
4. Gradual cutover
   - Increment traffic in 10–25% increments with SLO gates.
5. Post-cutover stabilization
   - 72-hour intensive monitoring, tuning, and a final retrospective.
slo_gates_and_success_criteria:
- Latency: p95 Dedicated <= hosted p95 * 1.10 (10% buffer).
- Error rate: total request error rate < 0.1% sustained.
- Cost per effective request: estimated within +/-15% of simulated projection.
- Functional parity: all model outputs match acceptance prompt set (see QA checklist).
sizing_checklist:
- Peak concurrent requests (per-route).
- Expected steady-state QPS.
- Average and 99th percentile sequence length.
- KV cache hit rate expectations.
- Batching opportunity score (from optimizer).
- Compatible accelerator types and quantization profile selection.
api_and_compatibility_checklist:
1) API version pinning: ensure client uses API v3.
2) Model variant mapping: hosted model id -> dedicated model id mapping table.
3) Streaming: verify chunked responses over websocket/HTTP/GRPC as used.
4) Function calls: test tool invocation and structured JSON outputs.
5) Auth and key rotation: switch to Dedicated API key and verify RBAC roles.
6) Rate limits and quotas: update client-side throttles for Dedicated throughput targets.
billing_and_pricing_steps:
- Confirm customer's committed monthly tokens and burst policy.
- Map hosted metering to Dedicated reserved buckets (example table below).

Billing mapping example table:
| Metric | Hosted billing | Dedicated reserved mapping | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| tokens_generated | per-1k tokens | allocated token bucket | Overages billed monthly |
| embeddings_units | per-embedding | reserved embedding units | Retention tiering may apply |
| model_variant | variant surcharge | included/excluded per contract | Specify in order form |
networking_and_security_steps:
- For Private Dedicated: validate VPC routing, NAT, and egress rules.
- For Dedicated with peering: confirm allowed CIDR ranges and firewall rules.
- KMS: verify key policies and rotate test key.
- Audit logging: ensure Dedicated audit stream is active and destinations verified.
- Secrets: confirm no hard-coded hosted keys in customer infra.
observability_and_checklist:
- Dashboards: per-route latency, errors, token burn, cost per token.
- Traces: end-to-end trace sampling at 10% initially.
- Alerts (recommended):
  - p95 latency breach (> SLA threshold) — P1 page to oncall.
  - Error rate spike (>0.5% over baseline) — notify SRE and SE.
  - Cost burn anomaly (>30% over simulated baseline) — finance alert.
- QA prompt set: run daily automated fidelity checks against seeded prompts and record delta metrics.
runbook_steps_numbered:
1) Pre-cutover verification (SE + Customer): run 'smoke' script against staging dedicated endpoint.
2) Enable weighted routing at 5% to Dedicated and verify telemetry after 5 minutes.
3) Hold for 30 minutes; validate SLOs, logs, and QA prompt results.
4) Increase to 20% if SLOs pass; hold and validate.
5) Ramp to 50% then 100% with same validation windows.
6) Decommission hosted routes or keep fallback for 72 hours based on contract.
rollback_triggers_and_procedure:
Rollback triggers:
- sustained p95 latency > 150% of hosted baseline for 15 minutes,
- error rate > 1% for 10 minutes,
- critical functional regression on QA prompt set.

Rollback procedure:
1) Immediately switch routing back to hosted (zero downtime if weighted routing enabled).
2) Notify customer and stakeholders via escalation channel.
3) Capture full diagnostic bundle (traces, logs, kernel perf counters).
4) Open an incident with engineering and assign action items.
5) Resume migration only after root cause and mitigations validated.
testing_matrix:
- Unit: client SDK behavior with Dedicated endpoints (pass/fail).
- Integration: end-to-end generation with models used in production.
- Performance: sustained 1-hour soak at 120% expected production QPS.
- Fidelity: acceptance prompt set (50–200 prompts) — per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE/LLR where applicable.
- Security: penetration test on new networking configuration for Dedicated (basic report attached).
stakeholders_and_ownership:
- Primary owner: Solutions Engineering (SE).
- Delivery lead: Customer Success Manager (CSM).
- Runtime SRE: oncall during cutover window.
- Billing & Finance: subscription reconciliation and contract mapping.
- Product Manager: escalation and feature gating.
communication_and_customer_templates:
- Pre-migration email: template confirming cutover window, expected impact, rollback plan.
- In-window updates: cadence every 30 min during pilot and hourly during ramp.
- Post-migration report: include latency, errors, cost delta, and recommended tuning.
faq_and_known-issues:
Q: Will model outputs change after migration?
A: Functional parity is the goal, but small numeric differences can occur due to quantization or kernel differences. Use acceptance prompt set to detect.

Q: Can customers keep hosted as fallback permanently?
A: Yes, for a configurable period per contract; however, this may incur double-billing or reserved capacity retention fees.

Known issues: Some LLM ops that rely on microsecond-level timing (custom low-latency clients) may observe higher p99 variability on multi-tenant Dedicated pools; recommend dedicated accelerator families if low variance is required.
post_migration_tuning_guidance:
- Adjust batching windows and max tokens to optimize throughput.
- Re-evaluate quantization profile after 7 days with production traces.
- Tune cache TTLs for prefix/KV caches based on observed hit rates.
- Consider shifting cold-start models to lower-cost variant with graceful fallback for infrequent requests.
